newsitem.title: USA: Kmart Q1 gross margin 22.4 pct vs 22.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kmart Q1 gross margin 22.4 pct vs 22.6 pct.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday its gross margin for the first quarter was 22.4 percent of sales versus 22.6 percent last year.
"Kmart's earnings for the first quarter were on plan, with good balance between sales, gross margin and expense controls," said Floyd Hall, chairman, president and chief executive officer.

The discount store giant said selling, general and administrative expenses fell to $1.49 billion from $1.52 billion in the first quarter of 1996, resulting in an SG&A to sales ratio of 20.5 percent versus 21.8 percent.

"We saw solid performance in our Big Kmart high frequency conversions, and were very pleased with the introduction of the new Martha Stewart Everyday bed and bath lines," Hall said. "Product-line extensions for Martha Stewart and the new offering of our Sesame Street line of children's apparel this summer are also expected to enhance our customer appeal."

Kmart earlier reported net income of $14.0 million, or $0.03 a share, compared to a loss of $99.0 million, or $0.21 a share, in last year's first quarter. The year-ago period included discontinued operations charges of $63 million, or $0.13 per share, related to Kmart's investments in Thrifty PayLess Holdings, Inc. and Builders Square.
Kmart has 2,122 U.S. retail outlets and operates 123 stores internationally.
